headline: CopperCorp plans to raise up to C$3 million and shrink its share count
dek: The explorer's non-brokered placement pairs units and subscription receipts with a one-for-five share consolidation ahead of TSX Venture Exchange approval.
caption: Temperate forest in western Tasmania, Australia, where CopperCorp Resources is exploring for copper, gold and rare earth elements.

sources.title: CopperCorp Announces Non-Brokered Private Placement of up to C$3.0M and Share Consolidation

unverified_claims: Whether company insiders will in fact participate in the placement rests on the company's own statement that insiders 'may participate'; this is not yet confirmed.
brief: CopperCorp Resources, which is exploring for copper, gold and rare earth elements at its AMC project in western Tasmania, Australia, plans a non-brokered private placement of up to C$3.0 million. The raise combines up to 4,444,444 units at $0.1125 each, for up to $500,000, and up to 18,518,519 subscription receipts at $0.135 each, for up to $2.5 million.

Each unit carries one post-consolidation share and one warrant exercisable at $0.18 for 24 months; each subscription receipt converts, once escrow conditions clear, into a unit of one share and half a warrant exercisable at $0.24 for 24 months. The conversion depends on completion of the company's Skyline Project sale. Shares carry the usual four-month-and-a-day hold.

CopperCorp is also consolidating its shares on a one-for-five basis, cutting its roughly 118.96 million shares outstanding to about 23.79 million. The financing and consolidation remain subject to final TSX Venture Exchange approval, and proceeds are earmarked for exploration and drilling at the AMC project and for working capital.
body: CopperCorp Resources Inc. (TSXV: CPER; OTCQB: CPCPF), which is exploring for copper, gold and rare earth elements at its AMC project in western Tasmania, Australia, intends to raise up to C$3.0 million through a non-brokered private placement, the company said.

The offering's first tranche is up to 4,444,444 units priced at $0.1125 each, for gross proceeds of up to $500,000. Each unit is made up of one post-consolidation common share and one share purchase warrant, exercisable at $0.18 for 24 months from the date of issue.

The second tranche is up to 18,518,519 subscription receipts priced at $0.135 each, for gross proceeds of up to $2.5 million. Once escrow release conditions are satisfied, each receipt converts into a unit comprising one post-consolidation common share and one-half of a warrant, exercisable at $0.24 for 24 months. The conversion is contingent on completion of the sale of the company's Skyline Project, among other escrow conditions.

CopperCorp is also proceeding with a share consolidation on a one-for-five basis, reducing its roughly 118.96 million shares outstanding to approximately 23.79 million. Securities issued in the placement will be subject to the usual four-month-and-one-day resale hold. Company insiders may participate, which the company says will be treated as related-party transactions.

Proceeds are earmarked for exploration and drilling at the AMC project and for general corporate and working capital purposes, the company said. The offering and the share consolidation both remain subject to final acceptance by the TSX Venture Exchange, and finder's fees may be paid to eligible arm's-length parties under the exchange's policies. CopperCorp also trades on the OTCQB market in the United States under the symbol CPCPF.
